import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'bun:test';
import { setAuthSettings } from '@repo/auth';
import { db, team, workspace, workspaceManager } from '@repo/db';
import { signUpTestUser } from '#tests/helpers/auth';
import { authedApi } from '#tests/helpers/app';
import { resetDb } from '#tests/helpers/db';

describe('the workspace of a team', () => {
  beforeEach(resetDb);

  it('gives every account, the instance owner included, a workspace of its own', async () => {
    const first = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });
    const second = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });

    const managers = await db.select().from(workspaceManager);
    expect(managers).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(managers).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({ userId: first.userId, role: 'owner' }),
    );
    expect(managers).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({ userId: second.userId, role: 'owner' }),
    );
    expect(first.workspaceId).not.toBe(second.workspaceId);
  });

  it('gives the instance owner one while personal workspaces are off', async () => {
    await setAuthSettings({ personalWorkspaces: false });

    const first = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });
    const second = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });

    expect(first.workspaceId).not.toBeNull();
    expect(second.workspaceId).toBeNull();
  });

  it("puts each person's team in their own workspace", async () => {
    const first = await signUpTestUser();
    const second = await signUpTestUser();

    const teams = await db.select({ workspaceId: team.workspaceId }).from(team);
    expect(teams.map((row) => row.workspaceId).sort()).toEqual(
      [first.workspaceId!, second.workspaceId!].sort(),
    );
  });

  it('refuses a team that names no workspace', async () => {
    const owner = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });

    const refused = await authedApi(owner.cookie).teams.post({
      name: 'Design',
      slug: 'design',
    } as never);

    expect(refused.status).toBe(400);
  });

  it('lets only the workspace owner create a team', async () => {
    const owner = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });
    const member = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });
    const body = { name: 'Design', slug: 'design', workspaceId: owner.workspaceId! };

    const refused = await authedApi(member.cookie).teams.post(body);
    const created = await authedApi(owner.cookie).teams.post(body);

    expect(refused.status).toBe(403);
    expect(created.status).toBe(201);
  });

  it('refuses a team in a workspace the caller does not own', async () => {
    const owner = await signUpTestUser({ team: false });
    const [other] = await db.insert(workspace).values({ name: 'Other' }).returning();

    const refused = await authedApi(owner.cookie).teams.post({
      name: 'Design',
      slug: 'design',
      workspaceId: other!.id,
    });

    expect(refused.status).toBe(403);
  });
});

FILE: apps/web/AGENTS.md
================================================
# web (Next.js)

Next.js App Router. Pages server-render, API data loads in the browser. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui.

## Imports

- Imports within the same feature are relative (`./`, `../`). The shared layer and other features
  use the `@/` alias.
- A feature imports the shared layer (`@/utils`, `@/lib`, `@/hooks`, `@/context`, `@/services`,
  `@/i18n`, `@/components/*`), never another feature. One accepted one-way exception: `work-items`
  and `documents` may compose `issue` components (the read-only issue a public board or document
  opens). A second such need moves the piece to `components/common`.
- The shared layer never imports a feature. `app/` pages stay thin: mount the feature page and
  providers, or redirect.

## Feature structure

- **One component per file, no exceptions.** On finding a file with two, split it. File name =
  exported name, with the feature name as a PascalCase prefix.
- Split a component past ~120 lines or one that mixes layout, fetch, mutation and dialog.
- A feature's parts go in `components/`, `hooks/`, `context/`, `services/`, `utils/`, even when a
  folder holds one file. A React context and its `use*` reader go in `context/`. The feature root
  holds only entry components, one per page. No `pages/` folder.
- A feature with more than two pages gets one `components/<page>/` subfolder per page that has
  parts of its own. A part used by two pages goes in `components/` or `components/shared/`.
- Types live next to the code that produces them. A `types/` file is only for a shape with no
  single owner. Service files carry a `.service.ts` suffix.
- A part used by one feature stays in it. Promote it to the shared layer only when a second
  feature needs it.
- `src/lib` holds wrappers over external packages and the API client. `src/utils` holds own
  helpers with no external package behind them. `components/common` groups by purpose; imports of
  a sibling in the same folder are relative.

## Translations

next-intl, language from the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, then `Accept-Language`, no `[locale]` route
segment. Files are `messages/<locale>/<namespace>.json`; namespaces are domains, not pages.
`docs/dev/i18n.md` has the whole picture, including how to add a language.

- A new namespace needs its file in every language plus an entry in `coreMessages`.
- Do not subset messages with `pick()`: a missing namespace then fails at runtime.
- Angle brackets in a message are rich-text tags. Write `owner/repo`, not `<owner>/<repo>`.
- The layout mirrors for right-to-left languages. In new code use logical utilities (`ms`/`me`,
  `ps`/`pe`, `start`/`end`, `border-s`/`border-e`, `text-start`/`text-end`), not `ml-`, `left-` or
  `text-left`. A `left-1/2` centring pair stays physical: `translate-x` has no logical form.
- Content that is not prose sits in a `dir="ltr"` container. User-written text gets `dir="auto"`.

## Rules

- Read API data in the browser with the react-query hooks in `services/`. `lib/api` sends the
  browser cookie, so a server render cannot read as the user.
- A screen names itself in the browser tab with `useDocumentTitle`; a server-rendered page renders
  `components/common/DocumentTitle`. Never set `metadata.title` per route.
- A screen that has to stay live calls `useLiveRefresh({ scope, targets })` with a scope from
  `@/utils/revScopes`. Never its own polling.
- A paged list holds its window in `usePaging()` and renders `ListPager`. A filter change calls
  `reset()`.
- A "show more" list over a `Page<T>` route uses `useInfiniteQuery` with
  `getNextPageParam: nextPageParam` (`useCompletedCyclesQuery` is the shape to copy). A cursor
  route passes its own `nextCursor` or `nextPage`.
- A picker that needs every row calls a whole-list route (`/options` on a paged list), never a
  paged one with a large `pageSize`.
- The API client: `lib/api/core/` holds the transport, `mediaUrl` and the paging helpers,
  `lib/api/endpoints/` one flat file per domain, named after the module or sub-resource of
  `apps/api/src/modules` it calls, with its DTOs beside the functions.
- No `index.ts` or barrel under `lib/api`. Types cross domains with `import type`.
- A type named like a DOM global (`Permissions`, `Notification`) resolves to that global when its
  import is missing, and tsc fails only on a DTO-only field, so import it explicitly.
- Nothing per-instance may reach the bundle: the image serves every instance. New config of that
  kind goes in `utils/runtimeEnv`. Never `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` in a component.
- Avatars and attachments render from `/media/...` through `mediaUrl`, document assets from
  `/protected-media/...`. Both are on the web origin, never an absolute api url.
- **Every write tells the user how it went.** A failed `useMutation` is toasted by the
  `MutationCache`, so its call site adds nothing for the failure. A plain request or a better-auth
  call toasts its own.
- A call site adds `toast.success(...)` from `onSuccess` or after `await mutateAsync`, with a
  translated message, unless the screen already shows the result.
- A mutation that renders its own error sets `meta: { suppressErrorToast: true }`.
- **A reader gets values, not disabled controls.** When the user may not change a setting, render
  its state (icon plus word) instead of a disabled switch, input or button, and say once who can
  change it. Reuse `components/common/fields/OnOffStatus.tsx` for an on/off state.
- When a switch that gates a section is off, drop the section.
- A workspace's owner and admins reach its projects and teams without being members: the project
  or team carries `via: 'workspace'`. In a project `usePermissions().isMember` is false; a team
  screen reads `team.via`.
- For those users, leave out starring and hiding a project, saving a private view, leaving the
  project or the team, and notification settings. Everything else follows `can()`.
- Add shadcn components with `bunx shadcn@latest add <name>`.
- **Do not edit `src/components/ui/`.** Re-adding a component overwrites it. Style from outside:
  a rule in `globals.css` on `[data-slot='…']`, outside `@layer`, since anything in
  `@layer components` loses to utility classes. Prefer a prop the component exposes.
- After a re-add, re-apply the local edits. `chart.tsx`: `debounce` on `ResponsiveContainer`, or a
  chart in a resizing container loops until "Maximum update depth exceeded", and the `sized` gate.
- Local edits in other components: `sidebar.tsx` (translated labels, `isTypingTarget` on Ctrl+B),
  `calendar.tsx` (`useDateFnsLocale`), `command.tsx` and `message-scroller.tsx` (translated labels).
- Tailwind v4: no `tailwind.config`. Tokens are in `src/app/globals.css`.
- Do not remove `output: "standalone"` + `outputFileTracingRoot` from `next.config`: the Docker
  image depends on them.
- Guard `localStorage`/`window` in a render path with `typeof window === 'undefined'`. Client
  components still server-render. Read a stored value that reaches the markup in an effect, or the
  first client render does not match the server markup.

import { Suspense } from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import DocumentTitle from '@/components/common/DocumentTitle';
import BrandCardPage from '@/components/common/page/BrandCardPage';
import AuthLegalNotice from './AuthLegalNotice';

// The card shared by every logged-out screen. The forms read the URL (an invite
// parameter, a reset token, a "just confirmed" flag), so they render inside a
// Suspense boundary — useSearchParams needs one for these pages to prerender.
export default function AuthCard({
  screen,
  children,
}: {
  screen: 'signIn' | 'signUp' | 'forgotPassword' | 'resetPassword';
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const t = useTranslations('meta.screens');
  return (
    <BrandCardPage
      footer={
        <>
          <AuthLegalNotice />
          <DocumentTitle title={t(screen)} />
        </>
      }
    >
      <Suspense fallback={null}>{children}</Suspense>
    </BrandCardPage>
  );
}

'use client';

import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { PRIVACY_POLICY_URL, TERMS_URL } from '@/utils/app';

const linkClass = 'underline underline-offset-4 hover:text-foreground';

// Sits under the card on every logged-out screen. Google requires the privacy policy
// and terms registered for the OAuth client to be reachable from where sign-in
// starts, so this stays visible next to the "Continue with Google" button. An
// instance that does not configure the URLs (apps/web/.env) renders nothing.
export default function AuthLegalNotice() {
  const t = useTranslations('auth.legal');

  if (!TERMS_URL && !PRIVACY_POLICY_URL) return null;

  const key = TERMS_URL && PRIVACY_POLICY_URL ? 'both' : TERMS_URL ? 'termsOnly' : 'privacyOnly';

  return (
    <p className="text-center text-xs text-muted-foreground">
      {t.rich(key, {
        terms: (chunks) => (
          <a href={TERMS_URL} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className={linkClass}>
            {chunks}
          </a>
        ),
        privacy: (chunks) => (
          <a
            href={PRIVACY_POLICY_URL}
            target="_blank"
            rel="noopener noreferrer"
            className={linkClass}
          >
            {chunks}
          </a>
        ),
      })}
    </p>
  );
}

'use client';

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/forgot-password/AuthForgotPasswordForm.test.tsx
================================================
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, it } from 'node:test';
import { act } from 'react';
import type { Root } from 'react-dom/client';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from 'next-intl';
import { AppRouterContext } from 'next/dist/shared/lib/app-router-context.shared-runtime';
import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';
import { qk } from '@/services/queryKeys';
import auth from '../../../../../messages/en/auth.json';

// With password sign-in off the identity provider owns the password, so the recovery
// screen sends people there instead of asking for an address to mail a link to.
const replacedGlobals = [
  'window',
  'document',
  'navigator',
  'Node',
  'Element',
  'HTMLElement',
  'HTMLInputElement',
  'HTMLFormElement',
  'SVGElement',
  'Event',
  'MutationObserver',
  'getComputedStyle',
  'requestAnimationFrame',
  'cancelAnimationFrame',
  'localStorage',
  'fetch',
  'IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT',
] as const;

let dom: JSDOM;
let root: Root;
let client: QueryClient;
let originals: Map<string, PropertyDescriptor | undefined>;

const router = {
  push() {},
  replace() {},
  refresh() {},
  back() {},
  forward() {},
  prefetch() {},
};

async function render(config: Record<string, unknown> | null) {
  if (config) {
    client.setQueryData(qk.authConfig, {
      registration: 'invite',
      magicLink: false,
      google: false,
      oidc: true,
      oidcLabel: 'Company SSO',
      hasUsers: true,
      ...config,
    });
  }
  const { default: AuthForgotPasswordForm } = await import('./AuthForgotPasswordForm');
  await act(async () =>
    root.render(
      <AppRouterContext.Provider value={router as never}>
        <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
          <NextIntlClientProvider locale="en" messages={{ auth }} timeZone="UTC">
            <AuthForgotPasswordForm />
          </NextIntlClientProvider>
        </QueryClientProvider>
      </AppRouterContext.Provider>,
    ),
  );
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  originals = new Map(
    replacedGlobals.map((name) => [name, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, name)]),
  );
  dom = new JSDOM('<!doctype html><div id="root"></div>', {
    url: 'https://example.test/forgot-password',
    pretendToBeVisual: true,
  });
  for (const name of replacedGlobals) {
    if (name in dom.window) {
      Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, {
        configurable: true,
        value: dom.window[name as keyof typeof dom.window],
      });
    }
  }
  Object.defineProperties(globalThis, {
    getComputedStyle: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.getComputedStyle.bind(dom.window) },
    // The config request never answers, so a test without seeded config sees it loading.
    fetch: { configurable: true, value: () => new Promise(() => {}) },
    IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: { configurable: true, value: true },
  });
  Object.defineProperty(window, '__ITSAPLAN_ENV__', {
    value: { apiUrl: 'https://example.test', privacyUrl: '', termsUrl: '' },
  });
  client = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, staleTime: Infinity } } });
  const { createRoot } = await import('react-dom/client');
  root = createRoot(document.querySelector('#root')!);
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await act(async () => root.unmount());
  client.clear();
  dom.window.close();
  for (const [name, descriptor] of originals) {
    if (descriptor) Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, descriptor);
    else Reflect.deleteProperty(globalThis, name);
  }
});

describe('AuthForgotPasswordForm', () => {
  it('points to the identity provider when password sign-in is off', async () => {
    await render({ emailPassword: false });

    assert.equal(document.querySelector('#email'), null);
    assert.ok(document.body.textContent?.includes(auth.forgotPassword.subtitleSso));
    assert.ok(
      [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].some((b) => b.textContent?.includes('Company SSO')),
    );
  });

  it('asks for the address when password sign-in is on', async () => {
    await render({ emailPassword: true });

    assert.ok(document.querySelector('#email'));
  });

  it('asks for the address while the config loads', async () => {
    await render(null);

    assert.ok(document.querySelector('#email'));
  });
});

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/forgot-password/AuthForgotPasswordForm.tsx
================================================
'use client';

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import AuthFormHeader from '../AuthFormHeader';
import AuthMessagePanel from '../AuthMessagePanel';
import AuthRegisterProviders from '../AuthRegisterProviders';
import {
  sendPasswordResetEmail,
  signInWithGoogle,
  signInWithOidc,
} from '../../services/auth.service';
import { useAuthAction } from '../../hooks/useAuthAction';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';

// Asks for the address and mails a reset link. The answer is the same whether or not
// an account exists, so this screen never tells the visitor which it was.
export default function AuthForgotPasswordForm() {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [sent, setSent] = useState(false);
  const { error, pending, run } = useAuthAction();
  // The api mails no reset link while the password form is off: the identity provider
  // holds the password then.
  const passwordEnabled = useAuthConfig()?.emailPassword !== false;

  function onSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    run(
      async () => {
        await sendPasswordResetEmail(email);
        setSent(true);
      },
      { redirect: false },
    );
  }

  if (sent) {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('forgotPassword.sentTitle')}
        description={t('forgotPassword.sentDescription', { email })}
        footer={
          <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
            {t('forgotPassword.backToSignIn')}
          </Link>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  if (!passwordEnabled) {
    return (
      <div className="p-6 md:p-8">
        <FieldGroup>
          <AuthFormHeader
            title={t('forgotPassword.title')}
            description={t('forgotPassword.subtitleSso')}
          />

          <AuthRegisterProviders
            pending={pending}
            onOidc={() => run(signInWithOidc, { redirect: false })}
            onGoogle={() => run(signInWithGoogle, { redirect: false })}
          />

          {error && <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>}

          <FieldDescription className="text-center">
            {t('forgotPassword.remembered')}{' '}
            <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
              {t('forgotPassword.signIn')}
            </Link>
          </FieldDescription>
        </FieldGroup>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit} className="p-6 md:p-8">
      <FieldGroup>
        <AuthFormHeader
          title={t('forgotPassword.title')}
          description={t('forgotPassword.subtitle')}
        />

        <Field>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="email">{t('fields.email')}</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="email"
            type="email"
            placeholder={t('fields.emailPlaceholder')}
            autoComplete="email"
            required
            value={email}
            onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
            disabled={pending}
          />
        </Field>

        {error && <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>}

        <Field>
          <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>
            {pending ? t('forgotPassword.submitPending') : t('forgotPassword.submit')}
          </Button>
        </Field>

        <FieldDescription className="text-center">
          {t('forgotPassword.remembered')}{' '}
          <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
            {t('forgotPassword.signIn')}
          </Link>
        </FieldDescription>
      </FieldGroup>
    </form>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/login/AuthLoginAlternatives.tsx

'use client';

import { KeyRound, Lock, Mail, ShieldCheck } from 'lucide-react';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { SignInExtras } from '@/cloud';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Field } from '@/components/ui/field';
import GoogleIcon from '@/components/common/GoogleIcon';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';

// The sign-in methods that are not the email + password form: the magic link toggle,
// the instance's own OIDC provider, Google, and passkeys. Which of the first three
// show depends on the instance config. The invite screen has no magic link toggle, and
// passes the invited address as `email`.
export default function AuthLoginAlternatives({
  signingInWithLink = false,
  pending,
  email,
  onToggleMethod,
  onOidc,
  onGoogle,
  onPasskey,
}: {
  signingInWithLink?: boolean;
  pending: boolean;
  email?: string;
  onToggleMethod?: () => void;
  onOidc: () => void;
  onGoogle: () => void;
  onPasskey: () => void;
}) {
  const t = useTranslations('auth.login');
  const authConfig = useAuthConfig();
  // With the password form off there is no method to toggle away from, so the magic
  // link button would offer a screen the API refuses.
  const passwordEnabled = authConfig?.emailPassword !== false;

  // One Field for all of them so they sit together as a group — a Field each would
  // space them like separate form questions. Tighter than the default field gap:
  // they are one stack of choices, not separate answers.
  return (
    <Field className="gap-2">
      {onToggleMethod && authConfig?.magicLink && passwordEnabled && (
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" disabled={pending} onClick={onToggleMethod}>
          {signingInWithLink ? <Lock /> : <Mail />}
          {signingInWithLink ? t('withPassword') : t('withLink')}
        </Button>
      )}
      {authConfig?.oidc && (
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={onOidc} disabled={pending}>
          <ShieldCheck />
          {/* The operator named their own identity provider, so the label is shown
              as given rather than translated. */}
          {authConfig.oidcLabel || t('withSso')}
        </Button>
      )}
      <SignInExtras pending={pending} email={email} />
      {authConfig?.google && (
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={onGoogle} disabled={pending}>
          <GoogleIcon className="size-4" />
          {t('withGoogle')}
        </Button>
      )}
      <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={onPasskey} disabled={pending}>
        <KeyRound />
        {t('withPasskey')}
      </Button>
    </Field>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/login/AuthLoginForm.tsx
================================================
'use client';

import { useEffect, useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import {
  Field,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldGroup,
  FieldSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/field';
import AuthFormHeader from '../AuthFormHeader';
import AuthLoginAlternatives from './AuthLoginAlternatives';
import AuthLoginPasswordFields from './AuthLoginPasswordFields';
import AuthMessagePanel from '../AuthMessagePanel';
import AuthUnconfirmedNotice from './AuthUnconfirmedNotice';
import {
  EmailNotConfirmedError,
  isEmailAddress,
  resendVerificationEmail,
  sendMagicLink,
  signInWithPassword,
  signInWithGoogle,
  signInWithOidc,
  signInWithPasskey,
} from '../../services/auth.service';
import { useAuthAction } from '../../hooks/useAuthAction';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';
import { useRedirectError } from '../../hooks/useRedirectError';

// How the visitor is signing in. The screen holds one method at a time: with a
// password, or with a link mailed to the address. Passkeys stay available in both,
// since they need neither field.
type Method = 'password' | 'link';

// `title` replaces "Sign in" on a sign-in page under a name of its own (/login/<name>).
export default function AuthLoginForm({ title }: { title?: string }) {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');
  const [method, setMethod] = useState<Method>('password');
  // With a password this is either an address or a username; a sign-in link can only
  // go to an address.
  const [identifier, setIdentifier] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  // The address a sign-in link went to. Set on success, and it replaces the form:
  // there is nothing left to do on this screen until the inbox is opened.
  const [linkSentTo, setLinkSentTo] = useState<string | null>(null);
  // A confirmation email was re-sent. Inline, because the sign-in form stays useful.
  const [resent, setResent] = useState(false);
  // The last sign-in attempt was held back by the verification gate, so this screen
  // offers the confirmation link again.
  const [unconfirmed, setUnconfirmed] = useState(false);
  const { error, pending, setError, run } = useAuthAction();
  const authConfig = useAuthConfig();
  // An instance that runs entirely off its identity provider offers no form at all,
  // only the buttons below it.
  const passwordEnabled = authConfig?.emailPassword !== false;
  const params = useSearchParams();
  const justReset = params.get('reset') === '1';
  // `apiFailure` in lib/api/core/client.ts sends the browser here with ?expired=1 after the API
  // refused the session, so the screen can say why the user is back on it.
  const sessionExpired = params.get('expired') === '1';
  // A Google, OIDC or magic-link sign-in, or a confirmation link, that could not
  // complete comes back here as a redirect rather than as a rejected promise, so its
  // reason arrives in the query string.
  const redirectErrorMessage = useRedirectError();
  const redirectError = redirectErrorMessage(params.get('error'));
  // The confirmation link carries ?verified=1 and adds ?error=… when it failed, so
  // the success line only stands while there is no error next to it.
  const justVerified = params.get('verified') === '1' && !redirectError;

  const router = useRouter();
  // A fresh instance has nobody to sign in: the first account is created on sign-up.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (authConfig?.hasUsers === false) router.replace('/register');
  }, [authConfig?.hasUsers, router]);

  function switchTo(next: Method) {
    setMethod(next);
    setError(null);
    setUnconfirmed(false);
  }

  function onSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    setUnconfirmed(false);
    setResent(false);
    if (method === 'link') {
      run(
        async () => {
          await sendMagicLink(identifier);
          setLinkSentTo(identifier);
        },
        { redirect: false },
      );
      return;
    }
    run(async () => {
      try {
        await signInWithPassword({ identifier, password });
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof EmailNotConfirmedError) setUnconfirmed(true);
        throw err;
      }
    });
  }

  if (linkSentTo) {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('login.linkSentTitle')}
        description={t('login.linkSentDescription', { email: linkSentTo })}
        footer={
          <button
            type="button"
            className="underline underline-offset-4"
            onClick={() => {
              setLinkSentTo(null);
              switchTo('password');
            }}
          >
            {t('login.backToSignIn')}
          </button>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  const signingInWithLink = method === 'link';

  function subtitle() {
    if (sessionExpired) return t('login.subtitleExpired');
    if (justVerified) return t('login.subtitleVerified');
    if (justReset) return t('login.subtitleReset');
    if (!passwordEnabled) return t('login.subtitleSso');
    if (signingInWithLink) return t('login.subtitleLink');
    return t('login.subtitlePassword');
  }

  function submitLabel() {
    if (signingInWithLink) return pending ? t('login.sendLinkPending') : t('login.sendLink');
    return pending ? t('login.submitPending') : t('login.submit');
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit} className="p-6 md:p-8">
      <FieldGroup>
        <AuthFormHeader title={title ?? t('login.title')} description={subtitle()} />

        {passwordEnabled && (
          <AuthLoginPasswordFields
            signingInWithLink={signingInWithLink}
            identifier={identifier}
            password={password}
            pending={pending}
            onIdentifierChange={setIdentifier}
            onPasswordChange={setPassword}
          />
        )}

        {(error || redirectError) && <FieldError>{error ?? redirectError}</FieldError>}

        {unconfirmed && (
          <AuthUnconfirmedNotice
            resent={resent}
            pending={pending}
            canResend={isEmailAddress(identifier)}
            onResend={() =>
              run(
                async () => {
                  await resendVerificationEmail(identifier);
                  setResent(true);
                },
                { redirect: false },
              )
            }
          />
        )}

        {passwordEnabled && (
          <>
            <Field>
              <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>
                {submitLabel()}
              </Button>
            </Field>

            <FieldSeparator>{t('login.or')}</FieldSeparator>
          </>
        )}

        <AuthLoginAlternatives
          signingInWithLink={signingInWithLink}
          pending={pending}
          onToggleMethod={() => switchTo(signingInWithLink ? 'password' : 'link')}
          onOidc={() => run(signInWithOidc, { redirect: false })}
          onGoogle={() => run(signInWithGoogle, { redirect: false })}
          onPasskey={() => run(signInWithPasskey, { fallback: t('errors.passkey') })}
        />

        {/* Only when anyone can register with a password. An invite-only instance
            hands out links directly, a closed one has nowhere to send the visitor,
            and with single sign-on the identity provider makes the account. */}
        {authConfig?.registration === 'open' && passwordEnabled && (
          <FieldDescription className="text-center">
            {t('login.noAccount')}{' '}
            <Link href="/register" className="underline underline-offset-4">
              {t('login.signUp')}
            </Link>
          </FieldDescription>
        )}
      </FieldGroup>
    </form>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/login/AuthLoginPasswordFields.tsx

'use client';

import Link from 'next/link';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';

// The identifier and password pair. With a password the identifier is an address or
// a username; a sign-in link can only go to an address, so the password field drops
// away and the label changes with it.
export default function AuthLoginPasswordFields({
  signingInWithLink,
  identifier,
  password,
  pending,
  onIdentifierChange,
  onPasswordChange,
}: {
  signingInWithLink: boolean;
  identifier: string;
  password: string;
  pending: boolean;
  onIdentifierChange: (value: string) => void;
  onPasswordChange: (value: string) => void;
}) {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');
  const authConfig = useAuthConfig();

  return (
    <>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="identifier">
          {signingInWithLink ? t('fields.email') : t('fields.identifier')}
        </FieldLabel>
        <Input
          id="identifier"
          type={signingInWithLink ? 'email' : 'text'}
          placeholder={t('fields.emailPlaceholder')}
          autoComplete="username"
          required
          value={identifier}
          onChange={(e) => onIdentifierChange(e.target.value)}
          disabled={pending}
        />
      </Field>

      {!signingInWithLink && (
        <Field>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
            <FieldLabel htmlFor="password">{t('fields.password')}</FieldLabel>
            {authConfig?.emailEnabled && (
              <Link
                href="/forgot-password"
                className="text-sm text-muted-foreground underline-offset-4 hover:underline"
              >
                {t('login.forgotPassword')}
              </Link>
            )}
          </div>
          <Input
            id="password"
            type="password"
            autoComplete="current-password"
            required
            minLength={8}
            value={password}
            onChange={(e) => onPasswordChange(e.target.value)}
            disabled={pending}
          />
        </Field>
      )}
    </>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/login/AuthUnconfirmedNotice.tsx

'use client';

import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { FieldDescription } from '@/components/ui/field';

// Shown when a sign-in was refused because the address is still unconfirmed: point at
// the spam folder, and offer to send the confirmation link again. A sign-in by
// username gives no address to send to, so that case asks for one instead.
export default function AuthUnconfirmedNotice({
  resent,
  pending,
  canResend,
  onResend,
}: {
  resent: boolean;
  pending: boolean;
  canResend: boolean;
  onResend: () => void;
}) {
  const t = useTranslations('auth.login');

  return (
    <FieldDescription className="text-center">
      {resent && t('unconfirmedResent')}
      {!resent && !canResend && t('unconfirmedNeedsEmail')}
      {!resent &&
        canResend &&
        t.rich('unconfirmedPrompt', {
          resend: (chunks) => (
            <button
              type="button"
              className="underline underline-offset-4"
              disabled={pending}
              onClick={onResend}
            >
              {chunks}
            </button>
          ),
        })}
    </FieldDescription>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/register/AuthRegisterForm.test.tsx

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, it } from 'node:test';
import { act } from 'react';
import type { Root } from 'react-dom/client';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from 'next-intl';
import { AppRouterContext } from 'next/dist/shared/lib/app-router-context.shared-runtime';
import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';
import { qk } from '@/services/queryKeys';
import auth from '../../../../../messages/en/auth.json';

const replacedGlobals = [
  'window',
  'document',
  'navigator',
  'Node',
  'Element',
  'HTMLElement',
  'HTMLInputElement',
  'HTMLFormElement',
  'SVGElement',
  'Event',
  'MutationObserver',
  'getComputedStyle',
  'IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT',
] as const;

let dom: JSDOM;
let root: Root;
let client: QueryClient;
let originals: Map<string, PropertyDescriptor | undefined>;
let restore: (() => void) | undefined;

const { spyOn } = createRequire(import.meta.url)('bun:test') as {
  spyOn: (
    target: object,
    method: string,
  ) => {
    mockImplementation: (implementation: () => Promise<unknown>) => { mockRestore: () => void };
  };
};

const router = { push() {}, replace() {}, refresh() {}, back() {}, forward() {}, prefetch() {} };

async function render(passwordEnabled: boolean) {
  client.setQueryData(qk.authConfig, {
    registration: 'open',
    emailPassword: passwordEnabled,
    hasUsers: true,
    google: false,
    oidc: true,
    oidcLabel: 'Company SSO',
  });
  const service = await import('../../services/auth.service');
  const spy = spyOn(service, 'signInWithOidc').mockImplementation(async () => {
    throw new service.AuthError('Too many requests', undefined, 429);
  });
  restore = () => spy.mockRestore();
  const { default: AuthRegisterForm } = await import('./AuthRegisterForm');
  await act(async () =>
    root.render(
      <AppRouterContext.Provider value={router as never}>
        <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
          <NextIntlClientProvider locale="en" messages={{ auth }} timeZone="UTC">
            <AuthRegisterForm />
          </NextIntlClientProvider>
        </QueryClientProvider>
      </AppRouterContext.Provider>,
    ),
  );
}

async function signInWithProvider() {
  const button = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(
    (one) => one.textContent === 'Company SSO',
  );
  assert.ok(button);
  await act(async () => button.click());
  assert.equal(button.disabled, false);
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  originals = new Map(
    replacedGlobals.map((name) => [name, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, name)]),
  );
  dom = new JSDOM('<!doctype html><div id="root"></div>', {
    url: 'https://example.test/register',
    pretendToBeVisual: true,
  });
  for (const name of replacedGlobals) {
    if (name in dom.window) {
      Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, {
        configurable: true,
        value: dom.window[name as keyof typeof dom.window],
      });
    }
  }
  Object.defineProperties(globalThis, {
    getComputedStyle: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.getComputedStyle.bind(dom.window) },
    IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: { configurable: true, value: true },
  });
  Object.defineProperty(window, '__ITSAPLAN_ENV__', {
    value: { apiUrl: 'https://example.test', privacyUrl: '', termsUrl: '' },
  });
  client = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, staleTime: Infinity } } });
  const { createRoot } = await import('react-dom/client');
  root = createRoot(document.querySelector('#root')!);
});

afterEach(async () => {
  restore?.();
  await act(async () => root.unmount());
  client.clear();
  dom.window.close();
  for (const [name, descriptor] of originals) {
    if (descriptor) Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, descriptor);
    else Reflect.deleteProperty(globalThis, name);
  }
});

describe('AuthRegisterForm', () => {
  it('shows a provider refusal when password sign-in is off', async () => {
    await render(false);
    assert.equal(document.querySelector('input[type="password"]'), null);

    await signInWithProvider();

    assert.equal(
      document.querySelector('[role="alert"]')?.textContent,
      auth.errors.tooManyRequests,
    );
  });

  it('shows the same refusal once above the submit button when password sign-in is on', async () => {
    await render(true);
    assert.ok(document.querySelector('input[type="password"]'));

    await signInWithProvider();

    const errors = document.querySelectorAll('[role="alert"]');
    assert.equal(errors.length, 1);
    assert.equal(errors[0]?.textContent, auth.errors.tooManyRequests);
    const submit = document.querySelector('button[type="submit"]');
    assert.ok(submit);
    assert.ok(
      errors[0]!.compareDocumentPosition(submit) & dom.window.Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING,
    );
  });
});

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/register/AuthRegisterForm.tsx

'use client';

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import {
  Field,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldGroup,
  FieldSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/field';
import AuthFormHeader from '../AuthFormHeader';
import AuthMessagePanel from '../AuthMessagePanel';
import AuthRegisterPasswordFields from './AuthRegisterPasswordFields';
import AuthRegisterProviders from '../AuthRegisterProviders';
import { signInWithGoogle, signInWithOidc, signUpWithEmail } from '../../services/auth.service';
import { useAuthAction } from '../../hooks/useAuthAction';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';

export default function AuthRegisterForm() {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [confirm, setConfirm] = useState('');
  const [awaitingConfirmation, setAwaitingConfirmation] = useState(false);
  const { error, pending, setError, run } = useAuthAction();
  const authConfig = useAuthConfig();
  const inviteOnly = authConfig?.registration === 'invite';
  const firstRun = authConfig?.hasUsers === false;
  const needsConfirmation = authConfig?.requireEmailVerification === true;
  // With the password form off, the identity provider is what creates the account,
  // so this screen keeps only the buttons that start that round trip.
  const passwordEnabled = authConfig?.emailPassword !== false;
  const hasProvider = authConfig?.oidc === true || authConfig?.google === true;

  function onSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    if (password !== confirm) {
      setError(t('errors.passwordsDoNotMatch'));
      return;
    }
    // With confirmation required, sign-up opens no session: the account exists but
    // stays unusable until the link in the email is opened.
    if (needsConfirmation) {
      run(
        async () => {
          await signUpWithEmail({ email, password });
          setAwaitingConfirmation(true);
        },
        { redirect: false },
      );
      return;
    }
    run(() => signUpWithEmail({ email, password }));
  }

  if (awaitingConfirmation) {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('register.confirmTitle')}
        description={t('register.confirmDescription', { email })}
        footer={
          <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
            {t('register.backToSignIn')}
          </Link>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  // Registration closed: the form has nothing to submit to. Invite-only still shows
  // the form — an invited address can sign up here, and the API rejects the rest.
  if (authConfig?.registration === 'closed') {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('register.closedTitle')}
        description={t('register.closedDescription')}
        footer={
          <>
            {t('register.haveAccount')}{' '}
            <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
              {t('register.signIn')}
            </Link>
          </>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  function subtitle() {
    if (firstRun) return t('register.subtitleFirstRun');
    if (!passwordEnabled) return t('register.subtitleSso');
    if (inviteOnly) return t('register.subtitleInviteOnly');
    return t('register.subtitle');
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit} className="p-6 md:p-8">
      <FieldGroup>
        <AuthFormHeader title={t('register.title')} description={subtitle()} />

        {passwordEnabled && (
          <AuthRegisterPasswordFields
            email={email}
            password={password}
            confirm={confirm}
            pending={pending}
            onEmailChange={setEmail}
            onPasswordChange={setPassword}
            onConfirmChange={setConfirm}
          />
        )}

        {error && <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>}

        {passwordEnabled && (
          <Field>
            <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>
              {pending ? t('register.submitPending') : t('register.submit')}
            </Button>
          </Field>
        )}

        {hasProvider && (
          <>
            {passwordEnabled && <FieldSeparator>{t('register.or')}</FieldSeparator>}
            <AuthRegisterProviders
              pending={pending}
              onOidc={() => run(signInWithOidc, { redirect: false })}
              onGoogle={() => run(signInWithGoogle, { redirect: false })}
            />
          </>
        )}

        {!firstRun && (
          <FieldDescription className="text-center">
            {t('register.haveAccount')}{' '}
            <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
              {t('register.signIn')}
            </Link>
          </FieldDescription>
        )}
      </FieldGroup>
    </form>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/register/AuthRegisterPasswordFields.tsx

'use client';

import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';

// The address and the two password fields. They are the whole email/password sign-up,
// so an instance that runs off its identity provider leaves them out entirely.
export default function AuthRegisterPasswordFields({
  email,
  password,
  confirm,
  pending,
  onEmailChange,
  onPasswordChange,
  onConfirmChange,
}: {
  email: string;
  password: string;
  confirm: string;
  pending: boolean;
  onEmailChange: (value: string) => void;
  onPasswordChange: (value: string) => void;
  onConfirmChange: (value: string) => void;
}) {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');

  return (
    <>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="email">{t('fields.email')}</FieldLabel>
        <Input
          id="email"
          type="email"
          placeholder={t('fields.emailPlaceholder')}
          autoComplete="email"
          required
          value={email}
          onChange={(e) => onEmailChange(e.target.value)}
          disabled={pending}
        />
      </Field>

      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="password">{t('fields.password')}</FieldLabel>
        <Input
          id="password"
          type="password"
          autoComplete="new-password"
          required
          minLength={8}
          value={password}
          onChange={(e) => onPasswordChange(e.target.value)}
          disabled={pending}
        />
        <FieldDescription>{t('fields.passwordHint')}</FieldDescription>
      </Field>

      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="confirm-password">{t('fields.confirmPassword')}</FieldLabel>
        <Input
          id="confirm-password"
          type="password"
          autoComplete="new-password"
          required
          minLength={8}
          value={confirm}
          onChange={(e) => onConfirmChange(e.target.value)}
          disabled={pending}
        />
      </Field>
    </>
  );
}

import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, it } from 'node:test';

import { SearchParamsContext } from 'next/dist/shared/lib/hooks-client-context.shared-runtime';
import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';
import { qk } from '@/services/queryKeys';
import auth from '../../../../../messages/en/auth.json';

// A reset link the server no longer accepts gets the dead-link screen and its way to a
// new link, not an error line under a form that cannot succeed.
const replacedGlobals = [
  'window',
  'document',
  'navigator',
  'Node',
  'Element',
  'HTMLElement',
  'HTMLInputElement',
  'HTMLFormElement',
  'SVGElement',
  'Event',
  'MutationObserver',
  'getComputedStyle',

let restore: (() => void) | undefined;

// Loading the test helper without Bun's globals preserves the web app's fetch type.
const { spyOn } = createRequire(import.meta.url)('bun:test') as {
  spyOn: (
    target: object,
    method: string,
  ) => {
    mockImplementation: (implementation: () => Promise<unknown>) => { mockRestore: () => void };
  };
};

const router = { push() {}, replace() {}, refresh() {}, back() {}, forward() {}, prefetch() {} };

async function refuseReset(code: string, message: string) {
  const authClient = await import('@/lib/auth-client');
  // better-auth captures fetch at module import, which can precede this fixture in a combined run.
  const spy = spyOn(authClient, 'resetPassword').mockImplementation(async () => ({
    data: null,
    error: { code, message, status: 400, statusText: 'BAD_REQUEST' },
  }));
  restore = () => spy.mockRestore();
}

async function submit() {
  const { default: AuthResetPasswordForm } = await import('./AuthResetPasswordForm');
  await act(async () =>
    root.render(
      <AppRouterContext.Provider value={router as never}>
        <SearchParamsContext.Provider
          value={new URLSearchParams('token=t1&email=ada@example.test') as never}
        >
          <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
            <NextIntlClientProvider locale="en" messages={{ auth }} timeZone="UTC">
              <AuthResetPasswordForm />
            </NextIntlClientProvider>
          </QueryClientProvider>
        </SearchParamsContext.Provider>
      </AppRouterContext.Provider>,
    ),
  );
  const fields = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="password"]');
  for (const field of fields) {
    await act(async () => {
      const setter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(
        dom.window.HTMLInputElement.prototype,
        'value',
      )!.set!;
      setter.call(field, 'new-password-123');
      field.dispatchEvent(new dom.window.Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
    });
  }
  await act(async () => {
    document.querySelector('form')!.requestSubmit();
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
  });
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  originals = new Map(
    replacedGlobals.map((name) => [name, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, name)]),
  );
  dom = new JSDOM('<!doctype html><div id="root"></div>', {
    url: 'https://example.test/reset-password?token=t1',
    pretendToBeVisual: true,
  });
  for (const name of replacedGlobals) {
    if (name in dom.window) {
      Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, {

        value: dom.window[name as keyof typeof dom.window],

  Object.defineProperties(globalThis, {
    getComputedStyle: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.getComputedStyle.bind(dom.window) },

  client = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, staleTime: Infinity } } });
  client.setQueryData(qk.authConfig, { emailPassword: true });
  const { createRoot } = await import('react-dom/client');

  await act(async () => root.unmount());

describe('AuthResetPasswordForm', () => {
  it('shows the dead-link screen when the link was already used or expired', async () => {
    await refuseReset('INVALID_TOKEN', 'Invalid token');
    await submit();

    assert.ok(document.body.textContent?.includes(auth.resetPassword.deadLinkDescription));
    assert.equal(document.querySelector('form'), null);

  });

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/reset-password/AuthResetPasswordForm.tsx

'use client';

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { useAuthConfig } from '@/services/authConfig.service';
import AuthFormHeader from '../AuthFormHeader';
import AuthMessagePanel from '../AuthMessagePanel';
import { AuthError, setNewPassword } from '../../services/auth.service';
import { useAuthAction } from '../../hooks/useAuthAction';

const DEAD_LINK_CODES = new Set(['INVALID_TOKEN', 'USER_NOT_FOUND']);

// The screen the reset link opens. better-auth redirects here with ?token= when the
// token is valid, and with ?error= when it expired or was already used.
export default function AuthResetPasswordForm() {
  const t = useTranslations('auth');
  const params = useSearchParams();
  const router = useRouter();
  const token = params.get('token') ?? '';
  const email = params.get('email') ?? '';
  const linkError = params.get('error');
  // The api refuses /reset-password while the password form is off, so a link issued
  // before it was turned off must not offer a password field.
  const passwordEnabled = useAuthConfig()?.emailPassword !== false;

  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [confirm, setConfirm] = useState('');
  // The link was used, expired or names an account that is gone: the same dead-link
  // screen as a link that arrives broken.
  const [linkDead, setLinkDead] = useState(false);
  const { error, pending, setError, run } = useAuthAction();

  function onSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    if (password !== confirm) {
      setError(t('errors.passwordsDoNotMatch'));
      return;
    }
    run(
      async () => {
        try {
          const { signedIn } = await setNewPassword({ token, email, newPassword: password });
          router.push(signedIn ? '/' : '/login?reset=1');
          router.refresh();
        } catch (err) {
          if (err instanceof AuthError && DEAD_LINK_CODES.has(err.code ?? '')) {
            setLinkDead(true);
            return;
          }
          throw err;
        }
      },
      { redirect: false },
    );
  }

  if (!passwordEnabled) {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('resetPassword.deadLinkTitle')}
        description={t('errors.passwordDisabled')}
        footer={
          <Link href="/login" className="underline underline-offset-4">
            {t('forgotPassword.backToSignIn')}
          </Link>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  if (!token || linkError || linkDead) {
    return (
      <AuthMessagePanel
        title={t('resetPassword.deadLinkTitle')}
        description={t('resetPassword.deadLinkDescription')}
        footer={
          <Link href="/forgot-password" className="underline underline-offset-4">
            {t('resetPassword.sendNewLink')}
          </Link>
        }
      />
    );
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit} className="p-6 md:p-8">
      <FieldGroup>
        <AuthFormHeader
          title={t('resetPassword.title')}
          description={t('resetPassword.subtitle')}
        />

        <Field>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="password">{t('fields.newPassword')}</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="password"
            type="password"
            autoComplete="new-password"
            required
            minLength={8}
            value={password}
            onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
            disabled={pending}
          />
          <FieldDescription>{t('fields.passwordHint')}</FieldDescription>
        </Field>

        <Field>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="confirm-password">{t('fields.confirmPassword')}</FieldLabel>
          <Input
            id="confirm-password"
            type="password"
            autoComplete="new-password"
            required
            minLength={8}
            value={confirm}
            onChange={(e) => setConfirm(e.target.value)}
            disabled={pending}
          />
        </Field>

        {error && <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>}

        <Field>
          <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>
            {pending ? t('resetPassword.submitPending') : t('resetPassword.submit')}
          </Button>
        </Field>
      </FieldGroup>
    </form>
  );
}

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/hooks/useAuthAction.ts
================================================
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import { useRefusalMessage } from '@/hooks/useRefusalMessage';

// Runs an auth action while tracking pending + error, and redirects into the
// planner on success. `setError` is exposed so a form can report client-side
// validation before calling `run`.
//
// Actions that only send an email (reset link, sign-in link, confirmation) end on
// the same screen with a "check your inbox" message instead, so they pass
// `redirect: false` and keep `pending` cleared.
//
// A failure is worded by useRefusalMessage; `fallback` is the text for a refusal it
// cannot name, shown instead of the server's English message.
export function useAuthAction() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const refusalMessage = useRefusalMessage();
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);

  async function run(
    action: () => Promise<void>,
    options?: { redirect?: boolean; fallback?: string },
  ) {
    setError(null);
    setPending(true);
    try {
      await action();
      if (options?.redirect === false) {
        setPending(false);
        return;
      }
      router.push('/');
      router.refresh();
    } catch (err) {
      setError(refusalMessage(err, options?.fallback));
      setPending(false);
    }
  }

  return { error, pending, setError, run };
}

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, it } from 'node:test';
import { act } from 'react';
import type { Root } from 'react-dom/client';
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from 'next-intl';
import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';
import auth from '../../../../messages/en/auth.json';
import { useRedirectError } from './useRedirectError';

const replacedGlobals = [
  'window',
  'document',
  'navigator',
  'HTMLElement',
  'IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT',
] as const;
let dom: JSDOM;
let root: Root;
let originalGlobalDescriptors: Map<string, PropertyDescriptor | undefined>;

function Message({ error }: { error: string }) {
  return <p>{useRedirectError()(error)}</p>;
}

function render(error: string, messages = { auth }): string {
  act(() =>
    root.render(
      <NextIntlClientProvider locale="en" messages={messages} timeZone="UTC">
        <Message error={error} />
      </NextIntlClientProvider>,
    ),
  );
  return document.querySelector('p')?.textContent ?? '';
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  originalGlobalDescriptors = new Map(
    replacedGlobals.map((name) => [name, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, name)]),
  );
  dom = new JSDOM('<!doctype html><div id="root"></div>', { url: 'https://example.test/login' });
  Object.defineProperties(globalThis, {
    window: { configurable: true, value: dom.window },
    document: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.document },
    navigator: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.navigator },
    HTMLElement: { configurable: true, value: dom.window.HTMLElement },
    IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: { configurable: true, value: true },
  });
  const { createRoot } = await import('react-dom/client');
  const element = document.querySelector('#root');
  assert.ok(element);
  root = createRoot(element);
});

afterEach(() => {
  act(() => root.unmount());
  dom.window.close();
  for (const [name, descriptor] of originalGlobalDescriptors) {
    if (descriptor) Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, descriptor);
    else Reflect.deleteProperty(globalThis, name);
  }
});

// The ?error= values are the ones the api's registration-refusal-redirect test pins.
describe('useRedirectError', () => {
  it('names a closed registration', () => {
    assert.equal(render('REGISTRATION_CLOSED'), auth.errors.registrationClosed);
  });

  it('names an invite-only instance', () => {
    assert.equal(render('INVITE_ONLY'), auth.errors.inviteOnly);
  });

  it("names a build's own code by the text the build gives it", () => {
    const text = 'Sign out at your identity provider, then try again.';
    const messages = { auth: { ...auth, errors: { ...auth.errors, codes: { BUILD_CODE: text } } } };
    assert.equal(render('BUILD_CODE', messages), text);
  });

  it('shows the generic text for an unknown error', () => {
    assert.equal(render('something_else'), auth.errors.generic);
  });

  it('shows the generic text for a code named like an object property', () => {
    assert.equal(render('toString'), auth.errors.generic);
    assert.equal(render('constructor'), auth.errors.generic);
  });

  it('names an MCP authorization for a client the instance does not know', () => {
    assert.equal(render('invalid_client'), auth.errors.oauthClientUnknown);
    assert.equal(render('invalid_redirect'), auth.errors.oauthRedirectUnknown);
    assert.equal(render('client_disabled'), auth.errors.oauthClientRefused);
    assert.equal(render('unauthorized_client'), auth.errors.oauthClientRefused);
  });
});

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/hooks/useRedirectError.ts
================================================
'use client';

import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { AUTH_REFUSAL_KEYS } from '@/utils/authRefusals';

// Some auth failures reach the sign-in screen as a redirect rather than a rejected
// promise, and carry their reason in ?error=<code>. Five flows land here: the Google
// round trip, the OIDC one, the magic link, the confirmation link from the address
// verification email, and an MCP authorization the api could not hand back to its
// client. The ones a visitor can act on are spelled out here, any other code gets the
// generic text. ?error_description is never shown: anyone can link to this screen with
// a text of their choosing, and better-auth passes a provider's description on as sent.
//
// Linking a provider account to an account whose email was never confirmed is refused
// unless the instance trusts provider addresses: anyone could have registered that
// address with a password before its owner arrived.
const MESSAGE_KEYS = {
  unable_to_link_account: 'linkRefused',
  account_not_linked: 'linkRefused',
  signup_disabled: 'signupDisabled',
  INVITE_EXPIRED: 'inviteExpired',
  OIDC_DISABLED: 'ssoDisabled',
  email_not_found: 'emailNotFound',
  // The confirmation link failed. better-auth redirects with these uppercase codes.
  TOKEN_EXPIRED: 'tokenExpired',
  INVALID_TOKEN: 'invalidToken',
  USER_NOT_FOUND: 'userNotFound',
  ...AUTH_REFUSAL_KEYS,
  // The client or its return address is unknown: a client can keep a registration the
  // instance has since lost, as an upgrade that drops the old ones does.
  invalid_client: 'oauthClientUnknown',
  invalid_redirect: 'oauthRedirectUnknown',
  client_disabled: 'oauthClientRefused',
  unauthorized_client: 'oauthClientRefused',
} as const;

export function useRedirectError() {
  const t = useTranslations('auth.errors');

  return function redirectErrorMessage(error: string | null): string | null {
    if (!error) return null;
    if (Object.hasOwn(MESSAGE_KEYS, error)) {
      return t(MESSAGE_KEYS[error as keyof typeof MESSAGE_KEYS]);
    }
    // A build that sends codes of its own names their texts under auth.errors.codes.
    const own = `codes.${error}` as Parameters<typeof t.has>[0];
    if (t.has(own)) return t(own);
    return t('generic');
  };
}

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import { AuthError, EmailNotConfirmedError, authError } from './auth.service';

describe('authError', () => {
  // The form words a refusal by these, since the server's message is English.
  it('keeps the code and the status of the refusal', () => {
    const error = authError({ code: 'INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD', message: 'Invalid', status: 401 });
    assert.ok(error instanceof AuthError);
    assert.equal(error.code, 'INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD');
    assert.equal(error.status, 401);
    assert.equal(error.message, 'Invalid');
  });

  // The sign-in form offers to send the confirmation link again only when the address
  // is what stopped the sign-in. The api answers 403 for other refusals too.
  it('reports an unconfirmed address', () => {
    const error = authError({
      code: 'EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED',
      message: 'Confirm your email address before signing in',
      status: 403,
    });
    assert.ok(error instanceof EmailNotConfirmedError);
  });

  it('does not report a deactivated account as unconfirmed', () => {
    const error = authError({
      code: 'ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED',
      message: 'This account is deactivated',
      status: 403,
    });
    assert.ok(!(error instanceof EmailNotConfirmedError));
  });

  it('does not report a disabled password form as unconfirmed', () => {
    const error = authError({
      code: 'PASSWORD_AUTH_DISABLED',
      message: 'Password sign-in is disabled on this instance',
      status: 403,
    });
    assert.ok(!(error instanceof EmailNotConfirmedError));
  });
});

FILE: apps/web/src/features/auth/services/auth.service.ts
================================================
import {
  signIn,
  signUp,
  requestPasswordReset,
  resetPassword,
  sendVerificationEmail,
} from '@/lib/auth-client';

// Where a link in an email lands the reader. The auth handler runs on the API
// origin, so every link it builds needs the web origin passed in explicitly —
// without it better-auth sends the reader back to the API, which renders nothing.
const appUrl = (path: string) =>
  typeof window === 'undefined' ? path : `${window.location.origin}${path}`;

// Each call throws an AuthError on failure; on success the session cookie is set and
// the proxy lets the user into the planner. The caller words the failure by its code
// and status, since the server's message is English.

// A refusal from the auth server, with better-auth's code and the HTTP status.
export class AuthError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly code?: string,
    readonly status?: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AuthError';
  }
}

// Sign-in was refused because the address is not confirmed yet. The verification gate
// in @repo/auth answers 403 with this code, as better-auth does; a deactivated account
// and a disabled password form are 403s too, and must not offer the link again.
export class EmailNotConfirmedError extends AuthError {}

export function authError(error: { message?: string; code?: string; status?: number }): AuthError {
  const { message = '', code, status } = error;
  return code === 'EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED'
    ? new EmailNotConfirmedError(message, code, status)
    : new AuthError(message, code, status);
}

// The sign-in screen has one field for two identifiers: an address goes to
// /sign-in/email, anything else to /sign-in/username. An address is the only thing
// that can carry an "@", so that is what tells them apart.
export function isEmailAddress(identifier: string): boolean {
  return identifier.includes('@');
}

export async function signInWithPassword(input: {
  identifier: string;
  password: string;
}): Promise<void> {
  const identifier = input.identifier.trim();
  const result = isEmailAddress(identifier)
    ? await signIn.email({ email: identifier, password: input.password })
    : await signIn.username({ username: identifier, password: input.password });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// autoSignIn (set in @repo/auth) signs the user in right after sign-up, unless the
// instance requires a confirmed address, in which case no session is opened. The
// display name is derived from the email; the planner does not use it yet.
// callbackURL is where the confirmation link lands when the instance sends one.
//
// On an invite-only instance the API rejects the sign-up unless the address has a
// pending project invite, with a code the form words.
export async function signUpWithEmail(input: { email: string; password: string }): Promise<void> {
  const result = await signUp.email({
    ...input,
    name: input.email.split('@')[0] || input.email,
    callbackURL: appUrl('/login?verified=1'),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// Sends the password reset link. The address is not confirmed to exist: better-auth
// answers the same either way, so this never reveals who has an account.
//
// The address is carried in redirectTo so the reset screen can sign the user in once
// the new password is set: better-auth keeps the query it is given and adds its own
// `token` to it.
export async function sendPasswordResetEmail(email: string): Promise<void> {
  const result = await requestPasswordReset({
    email,
    redirectTo: appUrl(`/reset-password?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}`),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// Consumes the token from the reset link, sets the new password, and signs the user
// in with it. The sign-in is best effort: an instance that requires a confirmed
// address refuses it, and the caller sends the reader to the sign-in screen instead.
export async function setNewPassword(input: {
  token: string;
  email: string;
  newPassword: string;
}): Promise<{ signedIn: boolean }> {
  const result = await resetPassword({ token: input.token, newPassword: input.newPassword });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
  if (!input.email) return { signedIn: false };
  const attempt = await signIn.email({ email: input.email, password: input.newPassword });
  return { signedIn: !attempt.error };
}

// Sends a one-time sign-in link. Rejected by the API when the instance has magic
// links turned off.
export async function sendMagicLink(email: string): Promise<void> {
  // A refused sign-up comes back to errorCallbackURL; on / it would be lost in the
  // redirect to the sign-in page.
  const result = await signIn.magicLink({
    email,
    callbackURL: appUrl('/'),
    errorCallbackURL: appUrl('/login'),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// Sends the address confirmation link again, for someone held back at sign-in.
export async function resendVerificationEmail(email: string): Promise<void> {
  const result = await sendVerificationEmail({
    email,
    callbackURL: appUrl('/login?verified=1'),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// Starts the Google round trip. Unlike every other call here this one navigates away
// instead of returning a result: better-auth redirects to Google, and Google comes
// back to the API callback, which then sends the browser to one of these two URLs.
// Both must be on the web origin — the handler runs on the API origin. `returnTo` is a
// web path both lead to instead, the invite screen for an invitee.
//
// It covers sign-up as well: an unknown address gets an account, subject to the
// instance registration mode, and a known one signs into the account it belongs to.
export async function signInWithGoogle(returnTo?: string): Promise<void> {
  const result = await signIn.social({
    provider: 'google',
    callbackURL: appUrl(returnTo ?? '/'),
    errorCallbackURL: appUrl(returnTo ?? '/login'),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

// Starts the round trip through the instance's own OIDC provider. Same shape as the
// Google call above: it navigates away, and both callback URLs must be on the web
// origin. The provider id is fixed — the instance has exactly one.
export async function signInWithOidc(returnTo?: string): Promise<void> {
  const result = await signIn.social({
    provider: 'oidc',
    callbackURL: appUrl(returnTo ?? '/'),
    errorCallbackURL: appUrl(returnTo ?? '/login'),
  });
  if (result.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

export async function signInWithPasskey(): Promise<void> {
  const result = await signIn.passkey();
  if (result?.error) throw authError(result.error);
}

import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import {
  type ActionDef,
  listQuickActions,
  createAction,
  updateAction,
  deleteAction,
  reorderActions,
} from '@/lib/api/endpoints/actions';
import { EMPTY_FILTER_SET, type FilterSet } from '@/utils/filters';
import { useOptimisticReorder } from '@/services/optimisticReorder';
import { qk } from '@/services/queryKeys';

// Coerces an action's jsonb blobs (opaque on the server) into the client shapes:
// a FilterSet condition (empty when missing/partial) and an effect object.
// Applied by the actions query and after a create/update.
export function normalizeAction(a: ActionDef): ActionDef {
  const conditions = (a.condition as FilterSet | undefined)?.conditions;
  return {
    ...a,
    condition: Array.isArray(conditions) ? { conditions } : EMPTY_FILTER_SET,
    effect: a.effect && typeof a.effect === 'object' ? a.effect : {},
  };
}

// Reads the member-accessible list, so the issue quick actions work for a member
// without the `actions` read permission. Managing actions still requires it.
export function useActionsQuery(projectKey: string | null) {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.actions(projectKey ?? ''),
    queryFn: () => listQuickActions(projectKey!),
    enabled: projectKey != null,
    select: (rows) => rows.map(normalizeAction),
  });
}

export function useCreateAction(projectKey: string | null) {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ input }: { input: Parameters<typeof createAction>[1] }) =>
      createAction(projectKey!, input),
    onSuccess: () => {
      if (projectKey) void qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: qk.actions(projectKey) });
    },
  });
}

export function useUpdateAction(projectKey: string | null) {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ id, input }: { id: number; input: Parameters<typeof updateAction>[1] }) =>
      updateAction(id, input),
    onSuccess: () => {
      if (projectKey) void qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: qk.actions(projectKey) });
    },
  });
}

export function useDeleteAction(projectKey: string | null) {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (id: number) => deleteAction(id),
    onSuccess: () => {
      if (projectKey) void qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: qk.actions(projectKey) });
    },
  });
}

export function useReorderActions(projectKey: string | null) {
  return useOptimisticReorder<ActionDef>(projectKey ? qk.actions(projectKey) : null, (orderedIds) =>
    reorderActions(projectKey!, orderedIds),
  );
}

// The runner queue's marker names the agents and their runners, so it goes to readers of the
// agents only. Anyone else polls.
export function useAgentScheduleRuns(projectKey: string, scheduleId: number | null) {
  const { can } = usePermissions();
  const readsAgents = can('ai_agents', 'read');
  useLiveRefresh({
    scope: scheduleId == null ? null : revScope.runnerQueue,
    targets: [qk.agentScheduleRuns(projectKey, scheduleId ?? 0)],
    enabled: readsAgents,
  });
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.agentScheduleRuns(projectKey, scheduleId ?? 0),
    queryFn: () => listAgentScheduleRuns(projectKey, scheduleId!),
    enabled: scheduleId != null,
    refetchInterval: readsAgents ? false : 5_000,
  });
}
